name: Fraunhofer
desc: The far-field diffraction plate from an optical bench — a coherent beam through a slit, a double slit, an N-slit grating, a circular iris or a hex stop, printing its true Fraunhofer pattern in real spectral orders where blue diffracts least and red flares widest, the mount turning and the iris breathing over minutes; switchable to a single-wavelength laser exposure, a schematic iso-intensity contour plot, an ironbow detector readout, or a Sabattier-solarized print with Mackie lines rimming every order.

energy.doc: plate exposure — how far into the faint high orders the print is pushed (master knob)

scale.doc: magnification of the far field — high = a few huge orders, low = many fine ones

density.doc: slits in the grating (2..10) / contour band count

hue.doc: source colour cast — tilts the 5-line spectrum and sets the laser wavelength in 'mono' (200=cool, 40=tungsten, 0=HeNe red)

x.doc: optical axis x on the plate

y.doc: optical axis y on the plate

spread.doc: slit spacing / slit width ratio — how far the orders fan apart

aperture.doc: aperture on the mount; 'auto' swaps it every section like a technician working through the box

seed.doc: bench seed — mount angle, drift phase, plate grain
